title: Rejected after a job interview
example_phrases: didn't get the job after the interview
they picked someone else for the position
got a rejection email from my dream company
the interview went badly and they said no
why does nobody want to hire me
I was so sure I'd get that job

applications.ma-5-20-a: This rejection can still move you forward: what you learn from it becomes part of your next application.
applications.ja-4-f: One no is a step on the path, not the end of it.
applications.sen-14-16-a: You controlled your preparation and effort, not their decision. Judge yourself by those.
applications.epi-ench-24-a: Your worth is not decided by one hiring panel.

exercise: Write down three things that went well in the interview and one to improve.
If you can, ask the company for brief feedback.
Send one new application today, while the lesson is fresh.

title: I lost my job
example_phrases: lost my job and don't know what to do
made redundant after years at the company

applications.ma-8-32-a: Losing a job blocks some plans, but not your ability to act sensibly and calmly from here.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can begin again. Many people rebuild after losing work.
applications.epi-ench-18-a: Even this can teach you something about what you want next.
applications.ma-7-7-a: Asking friends, family or an employment office for help is a strength, not a weakness.

exercise: Write down what you need in the next month: money, routine, support.
Tell one person you trust what happened.
Pick one small step for tomorrow, like updating your CV or calling an advice service.

title: A long job search and losing hope
example_phrases: been applying for months with no luck
hundreds of applications and no offers
I'm losing hope of ever finding work
nobody even replies to my applications
I'm tired of searching for a job

applications.ma-12-6-a: Keep applying even when it feels hopeless; each attempt makes you a little better at it.
applications.sen-50-7-a: A long search does not mean it will never work. Change is still possible.
applications.epi-1-15-a: Some things ripen slowly. This is hard, but not a verdict on you.
applications.sen-14-16-a: Measure your days by what you did, not by replies you cannot control.

exercise: Set a small daily target you control, like two good applications.
Each week, change one thing: your CV, where you look, or who you ask.
Plan one thing each day that has nothing to do with the search.

title: Criticized by my boss
example_phrases: my boss tore apart my work
my supervisor embarrassed me in a meeting
my boss is never satisfied with me
told off by my boss in front of everyone

applications.ma-6-21-a: If any of the criticism is true, it can help you. Take what is useful.
applications.ma-8-49-b: Being criticised is one thing. Deciding you are worthless because of it is a step you can skip.
applications.epi-2-14-a: Try to hear the feedback as information before you hear it as an insult.
applications.ma-4-20-a: Your work and your worth are not made smaller by one person's blame.

exercise: Write down exactly what was said, without adding your own story.
Sort it into what is fair, what is unfair, and what is unclear.
If something is unclear, ask a calm question about it tomorrow.

title: A rude or difficult coworker
example_phrases: a colleague is constantly rude to me
I can't stand someone at work
a toxic person in my team
someone at the office is always condescending
my coworker talks behind my back

applications.ma-2-1-a: Expect that you will meet this person today. Prepared, their rudeness hits less hard.
applications.ma-9-22-a: Their mind works much like yours, with its own worries and mistakes.
applications.ma-7-71-a: You cannot fix their faults, but you can decide how you behave.
applications.epi-3-21-a: Patience helps with everyday quirks. If it turns into bullying, telling a manager or HR is the right step.

exercise: Before work, picture a hard moment with them and how you want to respond.
Keep contact short, polite and in writing where it helps.
If it is bullying or harassment, write down dates and report it.

title: Someone took credit for my work
example_phrases: my colleague presented my idea as theirs
someone took credit for my project
nobody knows I did all the work
they got praised for what I did
I did the work and someone else got the recognition

applications.ma-11-4-a: The good work you did is real, even if someone else got the thanks.
applications.epi-3-24-e: Your progress shows in what you can do, and that stays with you.
applications.ma-5-25-a: Taking credit was their wrong. Your task is to act well, and you can also speak up.

exercise: Calmly write down what you did and when.
Talk to the person or your manager with facts, not accusations.
Next time, share your work in writing so your part is visible.

title: Passed over for a promotion
example_phrases: didn't get the promotion I deserved
passed over again for a raise
my younger colleague got promoted instead of me
I've been stuck at the same level for years
they gave the role to someone else

applications.ma-9-12-a: Keep doing good work without self pity; it builds your next chance.
applications.ja-6-c: You do not see everything the other person went through to get there.
applications.epi-ench-24-a: A title does not decide whether you are somebody.
applications.ma-8-47-b: If something can be improved, ask what it would take and work on it.

exercise: Ask your manager what would make you a strong candidate next time.
Pick one skill to build over the next three months.
Decide calmly whether this place still fits your goals.

title: Too much work, I'm overwhelmed
example_phrases: I have way too much on my plate
so much work I can't keep up
my to do list never ends
everything is due at the same time

applications.ma-4-24-b: Ask of each task: is this really necessary? Drop or delay what is not.
applications.ma-8-36-a: You do not have to carry the whole list at once. Deal with today.
applications.ma-3-12-a: One task at a time, with full attention, gets more done than rushing between them.
applications.epi-4-10-c: Chasing everything leaves you with nothing finished. Choose what matters most.

exercise: Write down everything on your mind.
Mark the three that truly matter today and do the first one now.
Tell someone honestly what cannot be done in time.

title: Burnt out and exhausted
example_phrases: exhausted from work all the time
I dread going to work every day
I feel empty and worn out
I can't do this job anymore, I'm drained

applications.sen-15-6-a: Your mind needs real rest, not only distraction.
applications.ma-8-51-a: A life with no room to breathe cannot last. Making room is not laziness.
applications.ma-4-24-a: Doing fewer, necessary things is a direct path back to calm.
applications.sen-50-4-a: Exhaustion that lasts is worth taking to a doctor early.

exercise: Name one thing you can drop or hand over this week.
Protect one hour each day for rest that truly relaxes you.
If you have felt this way for weeks, talk to a doctor.

title: I made a mistake at work
example_phrases: I messed up badly at my job
made an embarrassing error at work
my mistake cost the company money
I sent the wrong email to a client
can't stop thinking about the error I made
I feel stupid after a work mistake

applications.ma-8-17-a: Blame helps nothing. Fix the cause if you can, and the result if you cannot.
applications.sen-28-9-a: Admitting the mistake is the first step to fixing it.
applications.ma-5-9-a: You will slip up sometimes. Come back to your principles and keep going.
applications.ma-12-1-b: Once it is handled, let the past be past and act well now.

exercise: Write one sentence: what happened and what it affected.
Tell the people who need to know, with a suggested fix.
Note one change that makes it less likely to happen again.

title: Stuck in a job I don't like
example_phrases: I hate my job but can't leave
stuck in a job that makes me miserable
I need the money but my job is awful
every day at work feels the same
I'm trapped in a career I don't like
I want to quit but I can't
my job is sucking the life out of me

applications.ma-5-16-b: Even in a job you dislike, you can still live well and act well.
applications.ma-8-47-b: If you can change something, act instead of only complaining.
applications.ja-2-f: Building new skills is the part of the change that is within your reach.
applications.ma-4-31-a: There can be quiet contentment in doing even this work well, while you plan your next step.

exercise: Write down what exactly you dislike: the tasks, the people, or the pay.
Pick one small step toward a change, like a course or one conversation.
Find one part of today's work you can do well and take pride in.

title: My work feels pointless
example_phrases: what's the point of my job
I feel like a cog in a machine
I don't see the purpose of what I do all day

applications.ma-11-5-a: Whatever the job, your deeper work is being a good person while doing it.
applications.ja-4-c: If you have not found your big purpose yet, do today's task well. It builds strength.
applications.sen-60-4-a: Being useful to the people around you gives meaning to ordinary days.

exercise: Write down who your work helps, even indirectly.
Do one task today as well as you can, for its own sake.
Spend a little time this week on something that feels meaningful to you.

title: I feel like a fraud at work
example_phrases: everyone will find out I'm not good enough
imposter syndrome at my new job
I got lucky and don't belong here
I'm not as competent as people think
afraid they'll discover I don't know what I'm doing

applications.epi-3-19-a: Everyone starts as a beginner. Still learning does not make you a fraud.
applications.sen-104-25-a: Something new can feel impossible before you have done it a few times.
applications.ma-7-52-a: Others may be more skilled, but you can match anyone in effort and honesty.
applications.ja-4-g: Confidence comes from small successes. Notice the ones you already have.

exercise: List three things you did well in this job.
Ask one honest question about something you do not know yet.
Remember that most people feel this way at times.

title: Nervous about a presentation or speech
example_phrases: I have to give a speech and I'm terrified
nervous about presenting to the team
I'm scared to speak in front of a crowd
my hands shake when I present

applications.epi-2-13-a: Nerves are strongest where you have practised least. Rehearse out loud.
applications.sen-107-4-a: Picture the hard moments in advance, like a question you cannot answer, and they will be easier to meet.
applications.epi-3-26-a: Each time you speak despite the fear, your courage grows.
applications.ma-7-8-a: Do not let the talk spoil today. You will meet it tomorrow with the same mind you have now.

exercise: Rehearse the first two minutes out loud three times.
Breathe out slowly just before you begin.
Afterwards, note one thing that went better than you feared.

title: Afraid to change careers
example_phrases: I want to change careers but I'm scared
is it too late to start a new career
afraid to leave my safe job
I want to do something different with my life but fear failing
starting over in a new profession
scared to quit and try something new

applications.ma-7-18-a: Nothing grows without change. Your change can be part of that.
applications.sen-82-19-a: Fears you never look at quietly hold you back. Name yours.
applications.epi-ench-29-a: Look at what the new path really takes, then decide with open eyes.
applications.ma-8-6-a: Change is familiar to everyone who has ever grown. The new does not have to be feared.

exercise: Write down your fears and next to each one what you could do about it.
Talk to someone who already works in the field you want.
Take one small test step, like a course or a side project.

title: Taking a big risk, like starting a business
example_phrases: should I quit my job to start a business
taking a big leap and I'm scared
afraid to invest everything in my idea
big decision with a lot of risk
should I follow my dream or play it safe

applications.epi-ench-29-a: Consider what it really takes and what follows from it, then begin with open eyes.
applications.sen-91-3-a: Thinking through what could go wrong makes it less of a shock if it does.
applications.ja-5-b: Bigger goals ask for bigger sacrifices. Decide what you are willing to give.
applications.sen-85-28-a: Being brave about your business means weighing the real risks, not ignoring them or being frozen by them.

exercise: Write the worst realistic outcome and how you would recover from it.
Ask someone with experience to poke holes in your plan.
Decide on a test step with a limit you can afford.

title: Stressed about exams
example_phrases: I have finals next week and I'm panicking
so much to study, so little time
I'm afraid I'll fail the test

applications.epi-2-13-a: Worry shrinks with preparation. Every practice question helps.
applications.ma-3-12-a: Study one topic at a time, with full attention.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not carry the whole exam season at once. Deal with today's work.
applications.sen-13-4-a: The exam you imagine is usually worse than the real one.

exercise: Make a simple plan: which topic on which day.
Study in focused blocks with short breaks.
Sleep and eat properly. A rested mind remembers more.

title: I failed an exam
example_phrases: I studied hard and still failed
I didn't pass my driving test

applications.ma-5-9-a: Failing once does not mean giving up. Come back to it and keep going.
applications.ma-12-6-a: Keep practising what feels hopeless; skill grows with practice.
applications.ja-4-f: Failure is part of the path to doing well, not the end of it.
applications.sen-14-16-a: Judge yourself by your effort and what you learn, not only by one result.

exercise: Look at where you lost the most points.
Ask a teacher or classmate what helped them.
Plan the retake or next step in small, scheduled pieces.

title: I keep procrastinating
example_phrases: always leaving everything to the last minute
I waste the whole day avoiding my tasks
I know what to do but I don't do it

applications.sen-shortness-9-a: Each time you tell yourself you will start later, you are spending today. Start a small piece now.
applications.sen-50-9-a: Starting is the hardest part. Once you begin, it gets easier.
applications.ma-8-22-b: Instead of planning to start tomorrow, start a small piece today.
applications.epi-1-7-a: Ask honestly what excuse you are using, then answer it.

exercise: Pick the smallest possible first step.
Set a timer for 10 minutes and do only that step.
When the timer ends, decide if you want 10 more.

title: I can't focus
example_phrases: I get distracted all the time
I read the same page five times
I can't stay focused on one thing

applications.ma-3-12-a: Give your attention to the one task in front of you. Focus itself brings calm.
applications.ma-5-11-a: Ask often: what is my mind busy with right now? It brings you back.
applications.ma-8-22-a: This thought, this act, this word. That is enough to attend to.
applications.sen-35-4-a: Switching aims all the time is a sign of drift. Choose one and steer.

exercise: Put your phone in another room.
Work on one task for 25 minutes, then take 5 minutes off.
When your mind wanders, notice it kindly and come back.

title: Not sure what to study or do next
example_phrases: I don't know what to study
unsure what to do after school
I can't decide on a career path
everyone knows what they want except me
what should I do with my future
no idea which direction to take

applications.epi-ench-29-a: Look at what each path really involves day to day, not only how it sounds.
applications.ma-10-12-a: When you cannot see the way, ask good advisers. That is wisdom.
applications.ja-4-c: If you do not know your big purpose yet, doing today's task well still builds you.
applications.sen-121-3-a: Start by understanding what kind of person you are and what you need.

exercise: Write down what you enjoy, what you are good at, and what people need.
Talk to two people who study or work in fields you are curious about.
Choose a next step you can change later if it does not fit.

title: Frustrated by slow progress learning something
example_phrases: I practice every day and still suck
why am I so slow at learning
it feels like I'm not getting anywhere
progress is so slow it's discouraging

applications.epi-1-15-a: Growth takes time, like a fig that must flower and ripen.
applications.epi-4-8-b: Real progress is often hidden for a while, like a seed under the soil.
applications.epi-4-4-a: Think of a song or skill that felt impossible a few months ago and is easy now. That is your progress.
applications.ja-4-d: Strength grows through steady practice, like a muscle.

exercise: Compare yourself to where you were three months ago, not to experts.
Keep a short log of what you practised each day.
Pick one small skill to master this week.

title: Pressure from my parents' expectations
example_phrases: my parents expect too much from me
I'm afraid of disappointing my parents
pressure from my family to succeed
my parents want me to be a doctor
I'll never live up to what they want
my dad is never proud of me

applications.epi-ench-23-a: If you shape your life only to please someone, you lose your way. Be enough for yourself.
applications.ma-8-56-a: Their hopes are theirs. Your choices and your peace are yours.
applications.epi-2-18-c: Try to earn your own approval, not only theirs.
applications.ma-12-4-a: You can value their opinion without trusting it more than your own judgment.

exercise: Write down what you want, separate from what they want.
Tell them calmly, at a quiet moment, what matters to you.
Accept that they may need time to understand.

title: My partner broke up with me
example_phrases: we broke up after years together
she said she doesn't love me anymore
how do I get over a breakup

applications.sen-99-5-a: The good times you shared remain yours, even now.
applications.sen-polybius-16-a: This can hurt deeply without defeating you.
applications.ma-7-1-a: Countless people have been through this and found their way. It will pass.
applications.ma-10-14-a: Life gives and takes. Try to meet this with openness rather than bitterness.

exercise: Let yourself feel sad; it is a real loss.
Reach out to one friend today.
Fill one evening this week with something just for you.

title: I can't stop thinking about my ex
example_phrases: I miss my ex so much
I can't stop thinking about my ex
I keep checking my ex's profile
my ex moved on and I didn't
still in love with my ex
I dream about my ex every night

applications.ma-7-17-a: When the thought of them comes, speak to it gently: not now, please leave.
applications.ma-7-29-a: Bring yourself back to the present. Most of the pain lives in the past.
applications.ma-6-15-a: Everything flows on. Clinging to what has passed keeps the wound open.
applications.sen-marcia-8-a: Doing things you care about gives your mind a rest from them.

exercise: Mute or unfollow their profiles for a while.
When you think of them, name one thing you want for your own future.
Plan something to look forward to this week.

title: My partner cheated on me
example_phrases: I found out my husband was unfaithful
she betrayed me with another man
I discovered messages to another person

applications.ma-7-22-b: Their betrayal did not damage your character. That part of you is whole.
applications.ma-5-25-a: The wrong was theirs. Your task is to look after yourself and your next steps.
applications.epi-2-10-a: Revenge would hurt you too. Protect your peace instead.
applications.sen-polybius-16-a: The betrayal hurts, but it does not get to decide who you are or what you do next.

exercise: Give yourself time before any big decision.
Talk to a friend or a counsellor you trust.
Write down what you need now: space, answers, or support.

title: Jealousy in my relationship
example_phrases: I get jealous when my partner talks to others
I'm so insecure in my relationship
I'm afraid my partner will leave me for someone else
I get angry when she goes out without me

applications.ja-3-b: Suspicion and envy are like a small cell. Letting go opens the door.
applications.ma-12-19-a: When jealousy rises, name it: this is fear. Naming it gives you distance.
applications.sen-98-6-a: Fearing a loss can hurt as much as the loss. Enjoy what you have now.
applications.ma-8-49-a: Stick to the facts and notice the story you add on top.

exercise: When jealousy hits, wait before acting on it.
Write down the facts you know and the fears you are adding.
Talk to your partner about your feelings, not accusations.

title: We keep arguing
example_phrases: my partner and I keep arguing
every conversation turns into a fight
we argue about the same things
small things turn into big arguments

applications.sen-anger-2-34-a: A fight needs two people. You can stop being one of them.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-a: Try to see the issue from your partner's side before answering.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-b: Wait until the first heat cools before you continue the talk.
applications.ma-6-53-a: Really listen to what they are saying before you respond.

exercise: Agree on a pause word that stops the argument for 20 minutes.
Come back and let each person speak without interruption.
Focus on one issue, not every past one.

title: I give more than I get in my relationship
example_phrases: I always give more in my relationship
my partner doesn't put in effort
I feel unappreciated by my partner
I do everything and get nothing back
my partner takes me for granted

applications.ma-8-56-a: Your peace should not depend entirely on how much they give.
applications.epi-ench-23-a: Giving everything just to please someone can make you lose yourself.
applications.ma-7-73-a: Kindness is complete in itself, but it is fair to ask for fairness too.

exercise: Write down what you give and what you would like in return.
Tell your partner calmly what you need, using specific examples.
Notice how they respond over the next weeks.

title: Rejected by someone I like
example_phrases: the person I like rejected me
she said she just wants to be friends
my crush doesn't like me back
I confessed my feelings and got turned down
I got rejected on a date

applications.epi-ench-24-a: Being turned down does not make you a nobody.
applications.ma-7-57-a: Try to accept your life as it is unfolding, not only as you hoped.
applications.epi-2-18-c: Your own approval matters more than any one person's.
applications.sen-9-7-a: New connections, like new friendships, are worth sowing again.

exercise: Give yourself a few days to feel disappointed.
Thank yourself for having the courage to try.
Do something social this week, without pressure.

title: I want a partner and I'm still single
example_phrases: everyone is in a relationship except me
I want someone to love me

applications.sen-9-5-a: You can manage alone and still want company. Both are human.
applications.epi-ench-33-a: Be the person you want to be, alone or with someone.
applications.ma-7-57-a: Try to love your life as it is now, not only the one you imagine.
applications.sen-9-7-a: Connections grow like seeds. Keep sowing them.

exercise: Plan one thing this week that you enjoy doing alone.
Say yes to one social invitation.
Notice the people already in your life and reach out to one.

title: Going through a divorce

applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not try to carry the whole separation at once. Deal with today.
applications.ma-9-20-a: Carrying their wrongs around only burdens you.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The good years still happened, and they remain yours.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can rebuild your life, step by step.

exercise: Get practical advice on legal and money questions.
Lean on friends and family; you do not have to do this alone.
Keep one daily routine that steadies you.

title: A long distance relationship
example_phrases: my partner lives in another country
I miss my partner who is far away
we only see each other a few times a year
can a long distance relationship work
living apart from the one I love

applications.sen-55-11-a: Someone you carry in your heart is never truly absent.
applications.sen-marcia-10-a: Love the time together fully, knowing it is precious.
applications.ma-3-10-a: Live the moments you have now, even apart.

exercise: Schedule regular calls you both look forward to.
Plan the next visit so there is a date to hold on to.
Fill your days with your own life too.

title: Afraid to trust someone again
example_phrases: I can't trust anyone after being hurt
afraid of getting my heart broken again
I push people away to protect myself
my last relationship ruined my trust
I don't want to get hurt again
opening up to someone new scares me

applications.sen-polybius-16-a: You were wounded, but not overthrown.
applications.sen-82-19-a: Fears you never face keep you from moving forward.
applications.sen-3-2-b: Take time to get to know someone well before you trust them fully.
applications.ma-6-31-a: Old hurt can make new people look like old dangers. Look again at who is really in front of you.

exercise: Notice the fear without letting it decide for you.
Open up in small steps, and watch how the person responds.
Talk to a friend or counsellor about the old hurt.

title: My partner controls, threatens or hurts me
example_phrases: my partner controls everything I do
my partner checks my phone and won't let me see friends
my partner gets violent when angry
I feel trapped and scared in my relationship

applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help is not a weakness. Reaching out is a strong and wise step.
applications.sen-50-4-a: Do not wait to ask for help. The earlier, the better.
applications.epi-1-1-d: Someone may try to control you, but your will and your worth stay your own.
applications.ma-7-22-b: What they do does not make you less. Your character is still whole.

exercise: If you are in danger right now, call 112. To talk to someone, call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria) or find a helpline at findahelpline.com.
Tell someone you trust what is happening.
If you can, keep important documents and a phone in a safe place.

title: Conflict with my parents
example_phrases: I always fight with my parents
my mom and I can't get along
my parents criticize everything I do
my parents treat me like a child

applications.ma-9-22-a: Their minds work much like yours, with their own fears and habits.
applications.sen-anger-2-34-a: An argument needs two people. You can choose not to escalate.
applications.epi-ench-42-b: Understanding why they say what they say helps you stay calm.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-a: Try to see the conflict from their side for a moment.

exercise: Pick a calm moment to talk, not the middle of a fight.
Say what you feel and need, without blaming.
Agree on one small thing you can both do differently.

title: I can't forgive my parent
example_phrases: my mother hurt me as a child
I'm still angry at my parents for my childhood
my dad was never there for me
how do I forgive my parent

applications.ma-11-18-b: Anger about an old wrong can hurt you more than the wrong. Letting it go is for you, not for them.
applications.sen-anger-3-27-a: Anger often lasts longer than the hurt. You can loosen it in your own time.
applications.ma-7-22-b: What they did did not destroy who you are.
applications.ma-12-12-a: Understanding why they acted may help, but forgiving is your choice, and boundaries are fine.

exercise: Write down what happened and how it affected you, just for yourself.
Decide what contact feels safe and set that boundary.
Consider talking to a therapist about it.

title: A difficult brother or sister
example_phrases: my sister and I don't talk
my brother always puts me down
my sibling is jealous of me

applications.epi-3-21-a: Be patient with their moods, but you do not have to accept being mistreated.
applications.sen-anger-2-34-a: It takes two to fight. You can step out.
applications.ma-10-30-a: When their faults annoy you, think of your own similar ones.
applications.ma-6-6-a: The best answer to unkindness is not to become unkind yourself.

exercise: Before you meet, decide which topics you will not take up.
When it gets heated, pause or leave the room.
Look for one thing you can share without conflict.

title: Tension at family gatherings
example_phrases: holidays with my family are stressful
christmas always ends in a fight
my aunt always criticizes me at gatherings
I don't want to go home for the holidays

applications.ma-2-1-a: Expect the usual comments before you arrive. Expected, they lose their sting.
applications.ma-4-3-a: You can step back into your own mind for a moment, even at the table.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Deal with this one evening, not every family problem at once.
applications.epi-3-21-a: Patience with quirks is kind. Leaving early when it gets hurtful is fine too.

exercise: Decide in advance how long you will stay.
Plan a calm answer for the comment you always get.
Take short breaks outside if you need them.

title: Cut off from my family
example_phrases: I don't talk to my family anymore
I had to distance myself from my family
missing a family I can't be around

applications.ma-10-14-a: Life gives and takes away. You can grieve what you lost and still live well.
applications.ma-5-18-a: Distance from family is painful, and you have the strength to build a good life around it.
applications.sen-123-8-a: The people you choose to spend time with can become your family too.
applications.sen-55-11-a: The good memories you carry are still yours.

exercise: Let yourself feel the loss, even if the distance was the right choice.
Spend time with people who treat you well.
If you want to reconnect, think about what would need to change first.

title: Losing patience with my kids
example_phrases: I keep yelling at my kids
I lose my temper with my son
I feel like a bad parent

applications.epi-1-26-a: Anger rarely teaches children anything. Patience and example teach far more.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-b: When you feel it rising, pause until the first heat cools.
applications.ma-5-28-b: Calm explanation solves more than shouting.
applications.ma-5-9-a: When you do lose it, apologise and start again. That teaches them too.

exercise: When you feel anger rising, take three slow breaths before you speak.
Get down to their eye level and use a calm, low voice.
At night, forgive yourself and plan one thing to try tomorrow.

title: Overwhelmed as a new parent
example_phrases: I just had a baby and I'm overwhelmed
no sleep since the baby came
being a new mom is harder than I thought
I don't know what I'm doing as a parent
new dad and I feel lost
I miss my old life since becoming a parent

applications.ma-8-36-a: You do not have to handle all of parenthood at once. Just today.
applications.epi-3-19-a: Every parent starts as a beginner. There is no shame in learning.
applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help is not a weakness. Accept it when it is offered.
applications.sen-50-4-a: If low mood lasts, talk to a doctor early. It is common and treatable.

exercise: Ask one person for one specific kind of help this week.
Rest whenever you can, even for 20 minutes.
Notice one small thing you did well today.

title: Caring for a sick or aging parent
example_phrases: taking care of my sick mother
caring for my elderly parent is exhausting
watching my parent decline while caring for them
no time for myself because I care for my dad

applications.sen-68-7-a: Your own mind has sore spots too. Tend to them gently.
applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help with care is not failing. Share the load.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not carry the whole illness at once. Take today as it comes.
applications.sen-marcia-10-a: Love the time you have together, as fully as you can.

exercise: Ask family, friends or local services for regular help.
Keep one small daily thing that is only for you.
If you feel exhausted or low for weeks, see a doctor.

title: Watching a parent get old
example_phrases: my mom is not the same anymore
afraid of losing my parents someday
my parents need more help now
seeing my parents age makes me sad

applications.sen-marcia-10-a: Love them fully now. It makes the time together precious.
applications.ma-7-27-a: Notice what you still have with them and treasure it.
applications.sen-13-17-a: Do not wait for a better time to say and do what matters.

exercise: Plan a visit or call this week with no special reason.
Ask them about a memory from their life.
Talk with them about what help they might want.

title: Someone at home hurts or threatens me
example_phrases: I'm being hurt by a family member
there is violence in my house
I don't feel safe at home

applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help is not a weakness. Reaching out is the strong thing to do.
applications.sen-50-4-a: Do not wait to ask for help. The sooner, the better.
applications.epi-1-1-d: Someone may hurt you, but your worth and your will stay your own.
applications.ma-7-22-b: What they do does not make you less. Your character is still whole.

exercise: If you are in danger right now, call 112. To talk to someone, call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria) or find a helpline at findahelpline.com.
Tell a trusted adult, teacher, friend or doctor what is happening.
Know which place you could go to if you need to leave quickly.

title: I feel lonely
example_phrases: I have no one to talk to
I feel alone even around people

applications.sen-9-5-a: You can manage alone and still want friends. Seeking connection is natural.
applications.ma-7-1-a: Many people feel this way, more than you might think. You are less alone than it feels.
applications.sen-9-7-a: Friendships grow like seeds. Sow one today.
applications.sen-55-11-a: People you care about, even far away, are still with you.

exercise: Send one message to someone you have not talked to in a while.
Go once this week to a place with people: a class, a club, a café.
Be kind to yourself on the evenings you are alone.

title: New city, no friends yet
example_phrases: I moved and don't know anyone
hard to make friends as an adult
I'm alone in a new place
I left all my friends behind when I moved
starting from zero socially after moving

applications.sen-9-7-a: Making new friends is like sowing. It takes time before the harvest.
applications.sen-9-5-a: Being able to manage alone does not mean you should stay alone.
applications.ma-8-45-a: A new place does not have to change who you are.
applications.sen-55-11-a: Your old friends are still with you, even from far away.

exercise: Join one regular activity, like a sport, class or volunteer group.
Say yes to small invitations, even from people you barely know.
Call an old friend this week.

title: A friend betrayed me
example_phrases: my friend stabbed me in the back
my best friend lied to me
I found out my friend was talking about me
my friend went behind my back

applications.sen-3-2-b: Get to know people well before you trust them with everything.
applications.ma-9-20-a: Carrying their wrong around only burdens you.
applications.ma-7-22-b: Their betrayal says more about them than about you.

exercise: Give yourself time before you decide what to do.
Talk to them honestly if you want to understand.
Invest in the friends who have been loyal.

title: Friends drifting apart
example_phrases: my friends and I are drifting apart
my best friend doesn't call anymore
my friends have moved on without me
we have nothing in common anymore

applications.sen-9-7-a: Old friendships are a harvest. They can be tended again.
applications.sen-55-11-a: A friend you carry in your heart is never entirely gone.
applications.ma-4-36-a: Change is natural, and friendships change too.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The good times you shared stay yours.

exercise: Send a message to one friend you miss.
Suggest one simple plan, like a walk or a call.
Accept that some friendships fade, and value the ones that grow.

title: I was left out or not invited
example_phrases: my friends hung out without me
they made plans and didn't tell me
I saw photos of a party I wasn't invited to

applications.ma-8-49-b: Being left out once is a fact. Deciding nobody likes you is a story you add.
applications.ma-9-38-a: Perhaps you misread the situation. There may be a simple reason.
applications.epi-ench-24-a: Not being invited does not make you a nobody.
applications.sen-123-8-a: Spend more time with people who make you feel welcome.

exercise: Name the facts and the story you are telling yourself.
If it matters, ask a friend about it calmly.
Make your own plan and invite someone.

title: A friend wasn't there when I needed them
example_phrases: my friend wasn't there for me
nobody showed up when I needed them
I was there for them but they weren't there for me
my friend ignored me when I was struggling
when I needed help everyone disappeared
my friend didn't even ask how I was

applications.ma-9-38-a: They may have had reasons you do not know.
applications.ma-11-18-a: You have also let people down at times. Everyone does.
applications.sen-3-2-a: It helps to know which friends you can truly rely on.

exercise: Tell them calmly that you needed them.
Listen to their side before you judge.
Notice who was there, and thank them.

title: A friend who drains me
example_phrases: a friend who only calls when they need something
I feel exhausted after seeing my friend

applications.sen-123-8-a: The people you spend time with shape your mind. Choose with care.
applications.ma-8-56-a: Your peace does not have to depend on their mood.
applications.epi-3-21-a: Patience is kind, but boundaries are fine too.

exercise: Notice how you feel after seeing them.
Set a gentle limit, like shorter meetups.
Tell them honestly if something needs to change.

title: I'm anxious around people
example_phrases: I don't know what to say in conversations
I'm afraid people think I'm weird
I avoid people because of anxiety
I'm shy and it holds me back

applications.epi-2-13-a: We are most anxious where we are least practised. Small steps help.
applications.ma-2-8-a: Guessing what others think rarely helps. Pay attention to what you are doing.
applications.epi-3-26-a: Courage grows each time you go despite the fear.
applications.sen-13-4-a: The embarrassment you imagine is usually worse than what happens.

exercise: Pick one small social step, like greeting a neighbour.
Before you go, plan two easy questions to ask someone.
Afterwards, note one thing that went fine.

title: Jealous of my friends
example_phrases: my friend has everything I want
I'm envious of my friends' success
I can't be happy for my friend
my friend got engaged and I feel bitter
why do my friends have better lives

applications.epi-ench-19-b: If you find your good in your own choices, others' success takes nothing from you.
applications.ja-6-c: You do not see their struggles and failures.
applications.sen-94-69-a: Your friend's happy posts do not show their worries. You are comparing your whole life to their highlights.
applications.ma-7-52-a: You can match anyone in kindness and steadiness.

exercise: Notice the envy without judging yourself for it.
Say one honest congratulations.
Write down one thing you want, and one step toward it.

title: How do I support a grieving friend?
example_phrases: my friend's father died, what do I say
how can I help someone who is grieving
supporting a friend after a death
I don't know how to comfort my friend
what to say to someone who lost a loved one
my friend is mourning and I feel helpless

applications.epi-ench-16-a: Show sympathy and even grieve with them. Compassion matters most.
applications.sen-helvia-1-a: When grief is fresh, advice can wait. Just be there.
applications.ma-6-53-a: Really listen. Let them speak about the person they lost.
applications.ma-7-74-a: Helping a friend is good for both of you. Keep showing up.

exercise: Say simply: I am so sorry, I am here for you.
Offer specific help, like bringing food or running an errand.
Check in again weeks later, when others have stopped.

title: My mother or father died
example_phrases: grieving the death of my parent
I can't believe my mother is gone

applications.sen-polybius-18-b: Grieving your parent is right. Nobody should expect you to feel nothing.
applications.sen-marcia-1-a: The pain is sharpest now. Time will soften it, slowly.
applications.sen-polybius-5-a: Your mother or father would want to be remembered with warmth, not endless pain.
applications.sen-helvia-19-a: Let the people close to you share this with you.

exercise: Let the tears come when they come.
Tell one person a favourite memory of your parent.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: My grandparent died

applications.sen-99-5-a: The time you had with your grandparent stays yours.
applications.sen-63-7-a: In time, thinking of them will bring a smile as well as tears.
applications.sen-marcia-12-a: Alongside the sadness, there is room for gratitude for the years you shared.
applications.sen-polybius-18-b: It is right to grieve them, however old they were.

exercise: Write down three things they taught you.
Share a story about them with family.
Keep something of theirs close for a while.

title: A friend died
example_phrases: I can't believe my friend is gone

applications.sen-55-11-a: A friend you carry in your heart is never entirely gone.
applications.sen-marcia-7-a: Losing a friend shakes even the strongest. Feeling it is human.
applications.sen-helvia-19-a: Lean on the friends who are still here; you share this loss.
applications.sen-63-7-a: One day remembering them will feel warm as well as sad.

exercise: Reach out to someone else who knew them.
Write them a letter saying what you did not get to say.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: My partner died
example_phrases: I lost the love of my life

applications.sen-polybius-18-a: Grieve as much as you need to. Only the extra weight of worst case thoughts is worth setting down, gently.
applications.sen-marcia-8-b: This pain will not always be this sharp. It eases, little by little.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The life you built together remains part of you.
applications.sen-helvia-19-a: Let the people who love you come close now.

exercise: Accept help with meals, paperwork and daily tasks.
Keep a small daily routine, even a short walk.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: My pet died
example_phrases: I had to put my pet down
my dog was my best friend and now he's gone

applications.sen-polybius-18-b: It is right to grieve a pet. The bond was real.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The happy days with your animal stay with you.
applications.sen-63-7-a: With time, thinking of them will make you smile again.
applications.sen-marcia-1-a: The ache will soften as the weeks go by.

exercise: Let yourself be sad without explaining it to anyone.
Look at photos and remember a happy moment together.
Do something in their memory, like planting a flower.

title: Someone died suddenly
example_phrases: I never got to say goodbye
I'm in shock after an unexpected death

applications.sen-marcia-7-a: A sudden loss shakes anyone. Your shock is a human reaction.
applications.sen-polybius-1-a: You are not alone. Others have lived through this and found their way.
applications.sen-polybius-16-a: This can wound you deeply without defeating you.
applications.sen-marcia-1-a: For now, just get through each day. Time will slowly ease it.

exercise: Focus only on today: eat something, drink water, rest.
Tell someone close what happened and let them help.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: Someone I love is dying
example_phrases: watching someone I love die slowly
the doctors say there's nothing left to do
my friend doesn't have long to live
preparing to lose someone I love

applications.sen-marcia-10-a: Love them fully in the time that is left. It is precious.
applications.epi-ench-16-a: Sitting with them, even in silence, is a gift.
applications.sen-polybius-18-b: It is natural to grieve already. You do not have to be strong all the time.
applications.sen-helvia-19-a: Let others support you while you support them.

exercise: Say what you want to say: thank you, I love you, I forgive you.
Ask the care team what to expect, so you feel less afraid.
Take short breaks for yourself without guilt.

title: Guilt after someone died
example_phrases: I feel guilty since she died
I should have visited more before he died
I wasn't there when my dad died
I regret things I said before they passed
could I have prevented their death
guilt after losing a loved one
I never told her I loved her

applications.sen-polybius-5-a: The person you lost would want to be remembered with love, not with your pain.
applications.sen-14-16-a: Judge yourself by what you knew and intended then, not by what you know now.
applications.sen-63-7-a: In time, the memories can become sweet instead of heavy.
applications.ma-10-4-a: Do not turn the blame on yourself. Be as kind to yourself as you would be to a friend.

exercise: Write down what you wish you had said, as a letter to them.
Ask yourself what they would say to you now.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: The anniversary of a loss
example_phrases: a year since my mom died
the anniversary of his death is coming
birthdays are hard since she's gone
every year on this day I fall apart
holidays remind me of who I lost
the date of the loss is near

applications.sen-marcia-16-a: Let the date remind you of them, not only of the grief.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The good times you shared are still yours today.
applications.sen-marcia-8-b: Notice how the grief has changed since the first days. It eases, slowly.
applications.sen-polybius-1-a: Many people are thinking of someone they lost today. You are not alone.

exercise: Plan the day gently, with something comforting.
Do one thing in their memory: visit a place, cook their dish, light a candle.
Let someone know the day is hard for you.

title: We lost a pregnancy
example_phrases: I lost the baby at twelve weeks
grieving a baby I never met

applications.sen-polybius-18-b: Your grief is real and right, however early the loss.
applications.sen-marcia-7-a: Even the strongest people are shaken by this. It is not weakness.
applications.sen-helvia-19-a: Let your partner and the people close to you share this with you.
applications.sen-marcia-1-a: The pain will soften with time, even if that is hard to believe now.

exercise: Allow yourself to grieve, in your own way and time.
Talk to your doctor or midwife about your body and your feelings.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: I lost my home or things I loved
example_phrases: we lost everything in a flood
we had to leave our home

applications.sen-polybius-16-a: This loss can wound you without defeating you.
applications.ma-5-31-a: Remember how much you have already come through. That strength is still yours.
applications.sen-50-7-a: Even after a long struggle there is reason for hope. Rebuilding is possible.
applications.sen-99-5-a: The memories made in that home stay with you.

exercise: Write a list of what you need first: shelter, documents, money.
Ask for practical help from family, friends and local services.
Take it one step at a time.

title: I got a hard diagnosis
example_phrases: the doctor gave me bad news
I just got a serious diagnosis
told I have a chronic condition

applications.sen-13-13-a: When the future is uncertain, lean toward hope.
applications.ma-5-31-a: Think of how much you have already come through. That strength is still yours.
applications.sen-50-4-a: Work closely with your doctors. Asking questions early helps.
applications.ma-8-36-a: You do not have to face the whole illness at once. Just today.

exercise: Write down your questions for your next appointment.
Tell one person you trust and let them support you.
Plan one small thing you enjoy this week.

title: Living with chronic pain
example_phrases: I can't remember a day without pain

applications.ma-7-64-a: Pain has limits. Try not to make it bigger by imagining the worst.
applications.ma-8-28-a: Your mind can find some calm even on painful days.
applications.sen-68-7-a: Be gentle with yourself, body and mind.
applications.sen-50-7-a: Even after a long time, there is reason for hope. Keep looking for what helps.

exercise: Keep working with your doctor on a pain plan.
On a bad day, lower your goals and be kind to yourself.
Notice one good moment each day, however small.

title: Living with a long term illness
example_phrases: living with a long term illness
I'm always tired because of my condition
I can't do what I used to because I'm sick

applications.ma-5-31-a: You have already come through a lot. That is evidence of your strength.
applications.sen-50-7-a: Even after a long struggle, there is still good reason for hope.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Deal with today. Tomorrow you will meet tomorrow.
applications.sen-68-7-a: Treat your body and mind gently, like a friend who needs care.

exercise: Plan your energy: pick the one or two things that matter most today.
Stay in touch with your doctors and ask for support.
Find one other person who lives with something similar.

title: Waiting for test results
example_phrases: the doctor will call next week
I can't sleep until I hear from the doctor
waiting for news about my health
scared of what the results will say

applications.sen-13-10-a: The result is not here yet. Do not suffer it in advance.
applications.sen-13-13-a: While you do not know, give yourself the benefit of the doubt and lean toward hope.
applications.sen-13-4-a: The worst outcome you picture while waiting is usually not the one that comes.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Just get through today. It is more bearable than the whole future.

exercise: When the worry comes, say: I do not know yet.
Keep busy with something absorbing.
Have someone you can call when the result comes.

title: Scared of an operation
example_phrases: surgery next week and I'm terrified
what if the surgery goes wrong
I have to go to the hospital

applications.sen-13-4-a: The operation you imagine is usually worse than the real one.
applications.sen-13-13-a: Lean toward hope. Most operations go as planned.
applications.sen-107-4-a: Knowing what to expect makes it easier to face. Ask your doctors.
applications.ma-7-8-a: Let tomorrow be tomorrow. Today you only need to prepare.

exercise: Write down your questions and ask them before the day.
Prepare small comforts for afterwards.
On the day, breathe out slowly when you feel nervous.

title: Recovering from an injury
example_phrases: I can't play sports because of my injury
I got hurt and can't work
my knee injury is taking forever to heal

applications.epi-1-15-a: Healing takes time, like fruit that has to ripen.
applications.ma-5-31-a: You have come through hard things before. You will come through this.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can begin again. Your strength can come back step by step.
applications.ma-6-29-a: Do not let your spirit give up. You have more strength than you feel.

exercise: Follow your rehab plan, even on slow days.
Write down small improvements each week.
Find something you can still enjoy while you heal.

title: I can't sleep, my mind won't stop
example_phrases: my mind races when I lie down
I can't switch off my thoughts at night

applications.ma-5-2-a: A troubling thought is only a thought. You can set it aside and return to calm.
applications.ma-12-19-a: Name what is in your mind: worry, fear, a plan. Naming it gives distance.
applications.ma-7-17-a: Tell the thought gently: not now, please leave.
applications.ma-8-36-a: You do not have to solve your life tonight.

exercise: Write your worries on paper before bed and close the notebook.
Breathe in for 4 counts and out for 6, ten times.
If you cannot sleep for weeks, talk to a doctor.

title: I don't like how I look
example_phrases: I don't like how I look
I compare my body to others
I hate looking in the mirror

applications.ma-5-5-a: Kindness, honesty and courage do not depend on how you look.
applications.sen-94-69-a: Polished pictures hide real lives. Do not compare yourself to them.
applications.epi-ench-44-a: Your worth is not in your appearance.
applications.sen-68-7-a: Treat your body with care, not contempt.

exercise: Unfollow accounts that make you feel bad about yourself.
Name one thing your body allows you to do that you are thankful for.
If eating or weight worries take over, talk to a doctor.

title: I'm struggling with my mental health
example_phrases: my anxiety is out of control
I don't feel like myself anymore
I think I need help for my mental health
I feel numb all the time
my mental health is getting worse

applications.sen-50-4-a: Problems of the mind are easier to treat early. Please ask for help.
applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help is not weakness. Getting support is the strong thing to do.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Just today. You do not have to carry all of it at once.
applications.sen-50-7-a: Even after a long struggle, there is real reason for hope.

exercise: Talk to a doctor or therapist this week.
Tell one person you trust how you are really doing.
If the sadness feels too heavy to carry, talk to a doctor or call Telefonseelsorge on 142 (Austria). Other countries: findahelpline.com.

title: Constant worry about my health
example_phrases: I google my symptoms all the time
I'm convinced something is wrong with me
worried I have a serious illness
I can't stop worrying about my health

applications.sen-13-4-a: Most of what we fear never happens. We suffer more in imagination.
applications.sen-66-31-a: A twinge or a symptom can look like danger before it is checked. Let a doctor look before your mind decides.
applications.sen-13-9-a: When you do not know, a frightened mind fills the gaps with the worst guesses.
applications.sen-50-4-a: Let a doctor check what worries you, then trust the answer.

exercise: Limit symptom searching online to never, or once a week.
Write down the facts you actually know.
If the worry keeps returning, talk to a doctor or therapist about it.

title: I can't stop worrying about the future

applications.sen-13-4-a: The future you are worried about today is mostly made of guesses, and guesses are often worse than reality.
applications.ma-7-8-a: You do not need to solve tomorrow tonight. You will have the same strength when it comes.
applications.sen-13-10-b: Think of past worries that never came true. This one may well be the same.
applications.ma-7-29-a: Bring yourself back to now. Most suffering lives in the future.

exercise: Write down the worry, then one thing you can do about it today.
For the rest, say: that is for later.
Spend five minutes noticing what you see and hear right now.

title: I overthink everything
example_phrases: I replay conversations in my head
I worry about every little thing
stuck in my head all the time

applications.ma-12-19-a: Stop and name the thought. Naming it gives you some distance.
applications.ma-5-2-a: A thought is only a thought. You can set it down.
applications.ma-6-52-a: Not every thought needs an answer or a verdict. You can let some go unjudged.
applications.ma-8-49-a: When you loop over a situation, write down only what actually happened. Most of the loop is the story on top.

exercise: Give yourself 10 minutes of worry time, then stop.
Write the thought down and the facts next to it.
Move your body: a walk breaks the loop.

title: Afraid of failing
example_phrases: fear of failure stops me from trying
what if I'm not good enough
I don't start things because I might fail
I avoid challenges because I might fail

applications.ja-4-f: Failure is part of the path, not the end of it.
applications.sen-104-25-a: Something is not impossible just because you have not done it yet.
applications.epi-3-26-a: Train against the fear. Courage grows with practice.
applications.sen-82-19-a: Fears you never face quietly hold you back.

exercise: Write down the worst likely outcome and how you would handle it.
Take one small step anyway.
Afterwards, notice what you learned, whatever happened.

title: I don't know what's going to happen
example_phrases: I don't know what's going to happen
waiting for a decision that changes everything
so much uncertainty in my life

applications.epi-4-7-a: Know what is yours to manage and what is not. Then you can be ready for whatever comes.
applications.sen-13-10-b: Not knowing feels like bad news, but it is just not knowing yet.
applications.ma-3-10-a: The future is uncertain, but this moment is here to live in.
applications.sen-13-13-a: When you truly do not know, lean toward hope.

exercise: List what you can control and what you cannot.
Do one thing from the first list today.
For the second list, practise saying: I will deal with it when it comes.

title: I can't make a decision
example_phrases: afraid of making the wrong choice
I don't know which option to pick
I need to decide but I'm stuck

applications.epi-ench-29-a: Look at what each option really involves, then choose with open eyes.
applications.ma-10-12-a: Ask someone you trust. Good advice is wisdom, not weakness.
applications.epi-4-2-a: Being pulled in two directions stops you. Choose and commit.
applications.ma-8-16-a: If it turns out wrong, changing your mind later is still your free choice.

exercise: Write each option with its best and worst realistic outcome.
Ask: which would I regret not trying?
Set a deadline and decide then.

title: I feel panic and can't calm down
example_phrases: my heart is racing and I can't breathe
I feel like I'm losing control
my chest is tight and I'm scared

applications.ma-8-5-a: First, do not panic about the panic. It will pass. Then look at what you need to do.
applications.sen-66-31-a: The danger feels real, but often it is only the appearance of danger.
applications.ma-5-2-a: Notice the thought, set it aside, and come back to your breath.
applications.ma-8-36-b: Only this moment is here, and this moment can be borne.

exercise: Breathe out slowly, longer than you breathe in, for one minute.
Name five things you can see around you.
If panic keeps coming back, talk to a doctor. It is very treatable.

title: Afraid of what people will think
example_phrases: I care too much about others' opinions

applications.ma-2-8-a: Guessing what others think rarely helps. Focus on your own actions.
applications.ma-7-21-a: Soon everyone will forget. That can free you to be yourself.
applications.epi-ench-13-a: Growing often means looking foolish for a while. That is fine.
applications.ma-12-4-a: Trust your own opinion of yourself at least as much as theirs.

exercise: Write down what you fear people will think.
Ask: would I judge a friend for this?
Do the thing anyway, once, and notice what really happens.

title: I just got bad news
example_phrases: my world just turned upside down
I heard bad news and I'm shaken
the phone call I dreaded came
I don't know how to process this news

applications.epi-3-18-a: The news is outside your control, but your response is not.
applications.ma-8-5-a: First, do not panic. Then look steadily at what needs to be done.
applications.ma-8-49-a: Stick to the facts you know. Notice the story you add on top.
applications.ma-5-18-a: This news is heavy, and you can carry it one step at a time.

exercise: Sit down and breathe slowly for a minute.
Write down the facts and the first small step.
Call someone you trust.

title: Dreading something tomorrow
example_phrases: something I'm scared of is happening tomorrow
I have a hard conversation tomorrow
can't stop thinking about tomorrow's meeting
tomorrow is going to be awful

applications.ma-7-8-a: Do not let tomorrow spoil today. You will meet it with the same mind you have now.
applications.sen-13-10-a: It is not here yet. Do not suffer it twice.
applications.sen-13-4-a: Most of what we dread is worse in imagination than in real life.
applications.sen-107-4-a: Picture tomorrow's hard moment and how you will handle it. Then it is easier.

exercise: Prepare what you can for tomorrow, then stop.
Plan something kind for yourself after it.
Tonight, do something calming and go to bed on time.

title: Furious at another driver
example_phrases: an idiot driver ruined my morning
so angry at a stranger in traffic

applications.sen-anger-2-10-a: The other driver may simply not have seen you, like someone tripping in the dark.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-b: Let the first heat cool before you react.
applications.ma-10-30-a: You have probably made driving mistakes too.
applications.ma-7-29-b: Leave it on the road. Do not carry it into your day.

exercise: Breathe out slowly three times before doing anything.
Drive on; do not follow or confront.
When you arrive, notice if the anger is still worth keeping.

title: Someone insulted me
example_phrases: she made fun of me in front of others
someone was rude to my face
I can't get over what he said to me

applications.epi-ench-20-a: Words become insults only when you accept them as insults.
applications.sen-anger-3-25-a: Staying calm means they did not manage to shake you.
applications.ma-8-49-b: Hearing it is one thing. Deciding you are harmed is a step you can skip.
applications.ma-11-13-a: If they look down on you, that is their business. Yours is to act well.

exercise: Do not answer right away.
Ask: is any of it true? If not, let it go.
If it keeps happening, set a clear boundary or get help.

title: Someone was mean to me online
example_phrases: people are mean to me on social media
a stranger insulted me on the internet

applications.epi-ench-20-a: A comment hurts most when you accept it. You decide what it means.
applications.ma-9-27-a: Look at where the comment comes from. Often there is no reason to be troubled.
applications.ma-8-49-b: Reading it is one thing. Believing you are harmed is a step you can skip.
applications.sen-76-4-a: Scorn from strangers is not worth your attention.

exercise: Do not reply while you are upset.
Mute, block or report the person.
If it is bullying or threats, save screenshots and tell someone.

title: I can't let go of a grudge
example_phrases: I can't let go of a grudge
I still resent what they did
I keep thinking about how they wronged me

applications.ja-3-b: Holding resentment is like locking yourself in a small cell. Letting go opens the door.
applications.ma-11-18-b: The anger often hurts you more than the original wrong.
applications.sen-anger-3-27-a: The grudge has lasted longer than the hurt. You can set it down.
applications.ma-9-20-a: Carrying their wrong around only burdens you.

exercise: Write down what happened and what the grudge costs you.
Decide whether you want to talk to them or simply let it go.
Each time it comes back, say: I am putting this down.

title: I want revenge
example_phrases: I want them to suffer like I did
I want to hurt them back
how do I get back at them

applications.epi-2-10-a: Getting even would keep you tied to the person who hurt you, and hurt you again.
applications.ma-6-6-a: The best answer is to refuse to become like them.
applications.sen-anger-3-5-a: Revenge against the weak is cruel and against the strong is risky. Choose peace and protect yourself.
applications.sen-anger-3-12-c: While you are angry, do not act. Decide later.

exercise: Wait at least a day before doing anything.
Write down what you really need: safety, an apology, or distance.
Put your energy into your own life.

title: I lost my temper and regret it
example_phrases: I yelled at someone and regret it
I said things I didn't mean
my anger got the best of me

applications.ma-5-9-a: You slipped. Come back to your principles and keep going.
applications.sen-anger-3-36-a: Look back on the day kindly: what happened, and what can I do better next time?
applications.sen-anger-3-13-a: You cannot always stop the feeling, but you can learn to not let it decide.
applications.sen-28-9-a: Admitting it is the first step to fixing it.

exercise: Apologise simply, without excuses.
Notice what set you off, so you can see it coming.
Next time, leave the room before you speak.

title: I get defensive when criticized
example_phrases: I hate being told I'm wrong
I argue when people disagree with me
admitting I'm wrong is hard for me

applications.ma-6-21-a: Being shown you are wrong is a gift. The truth never harms you.
applications.ma-4-12-a: Changing your mind is a strength, not a defeat.
applications.epi-2-14-a: Try to hear feedback as information, not as an insult.
applications.epi-ench-46-b: When criticism stops upsetting you, you are making real progress.

exercise: When criticised, say only: thank you, let me think about it.
Later, write down what part might be true.
Choose one small thing to change.

title: Rude strangers and bad service
example_phrases: someone pushed past me without apologizing
a cashier was rude to me

applications.ma-2-1-a: Expect some rude people today. Expected, they bother you less.
applications.epi-4-8-a: You do not know what kind of day they are having.
applications.ma-9-42-a: There will always be rude people. Expecting otherwise sets you up for anger.

exercise: Take one slow breath before you answer.
Stay polite and brief.
Do not replay it later; let it go.

title: Everyone gets on my nerves
example_phrases: I have no patience for anyone

applications.ma-8-8-b: You can choose not to be upset by thoughtless people.
applications.ma-10-30-a: When others annoy you, remember your own faults.
applications.sen-15-6-a: Constant irritation is often a sign that your mind needs rest.
applications.ma-2-1-a: Expect people to be imperfect. It takes the surprise out of it.

exercise: Check the basics: sleep, food, stress.
Take a short break alone today.
Notice one kind thing someone does.

title: I was treated unfairly
example_phrases: it's not fair what happened to me
I was blamed for something I didn't do

applications.ma-5-25-a: The unfairness is their responsibility. Your task is to act well, and you can stand up for yourself.
applications.ma-8-32-a: Unfair events can block plans, but not your ability to act fairly and calmly.
applications.ma-9-20-a: Do not carry their wrong around longer than you need to.
applications.ma-8-17-a: Fix what you can, and let go of what you cannot.

exercise: Write down the facts calmly.
Decide if you want to complain, appeal or ask for help.
Do one thing today that has nothing to do with it.

title: I'm not good enough
example_phrases: nothing I do is good enough

applications.ma-5-5-a: You may lack some talents, but kindness, honesty and patience are open to you right now.
applications.epi-ench-24-a: The feeling of not being enough is about status and comparison. Your kindness and effort already count.
applications.epi-2-9-a: Simply living up to being a good human is a big task. Be patient with yourself.
applications.ma-7-59-a: The good you are looking for in yourself is already there. It grows when you use it.

exercise: Write down three things you did well this week, however small.
Ask: would I talk to a friend the way I talk to myself?
Do one kind thing today and notice it counts.

title: I'm too hard on myself
example_phrases: I beat myself up over everything
I can't forgive my own mistakes

applications.epi-1-11-a: Changing yourself takes time. Be patient with yourself.
applications.ma-10-4-a: When you get something wrong, correct it kindly, the way you would help a friend.
applications.ma-5-9-a: You will slip up. Come back to your principles without disgust.
applications.sen-68-7-a: Your mind has sore spots. Tend to them gently, not harshly.

exercise: When the critic speaks, write down what it says.
Rewrite it as a kind friend would say it.
End the day naming one thing you did well.

title: I keep comparing myself to others
example_phrases: instagram makes me feel bad about my life
I always compare myself to others
other people have it all together
why is everyone else so successful

applications.sen-94-69-a: Do not compare your inside to other people's outside.
applications.ja-6-c: You do not see their struggles. Compare your journey only to your own.
applications.ma-7-52-a: Others may be more skilled, but anyone can match them in kindness and steadiness.
applications.epi-ench-19-b: If your good is in your own choices, their success takes nothing from you.

exercise: Notice when you start comparing, and name it.
Compare yourself to who you were a year ago.
Spend less time on the apps that trigger it.

title: Everyone my age is ahead of me
example_phrases: everyone my age is married with kids
my friends own houses and I still rent
people younger than me have achieved more

applications.ja-6-c: Other people's timelines hide struggles you never see.
applications.sen-101-10-a: Instead of measuring your life against others, make today a good day on its own terms.
applications.ma-7-57-a: Love your life as it actually unfolds, not as a timeline says it should.
applications.sen-93-7-a: Choose to live actively from where you are now.

exercise: Write down what you have built, learned or survived so far.
Pick one goal that matters to you, not to others.
Take one step toward it this week.

title: I can't say no, I always please people
example_phrases: I agree to things I don't want to do
I need everyone to like me

applications.epi-ench-23-a: If you shape your life only to please others, you lose your way. Be enough for yourself.
applications.epi-2-18-c: Before saying yes to keep others happy, ask whether you would be proud of that yes.
applications.ma-8-53-a: Many of the people you try to please are struggling with their own approval. You can stop chasing theirs.
applications.ma-8-56-a: Their reactions are their business. Your peace does not have to depend on them.

exercise: Next time you are asked, say: let me think about it.
Practise one small, polite no this week.
Notice that people usually accept it.

title: I need likes and approval
example_phrases: I need likes to feel good
I feel bad when nobody praises me
I check how many likes I got
I need others to tell me I'm good

applications.ma-6-16-a: Public praise is mostly noise. Do not build your worth on it.
applications.ma-4-20-a: Praise does not make you better, and silence does not make you worse.
applications.ma-11-4-a: Doing good counts even without likes or thanks.

exercise: Post or share something without checking the reaction for a day.
Write down one thing you are proud of that nobody saw.
Notice how you feel after a day with less checking.

title: Nobody notices me

applications.ma-7-67-b: Being unnoticed does not cancel the good you do. It still matters, even unseen.
applications.epi-3-24-e: Your progress is real even if nobody sees it.
applications.epi-ench-24-a: Being overlooked does not make you a nobody.
applications.sen-9-7-a: Connections grow when you sow them. Reach out first.

exercise: Start one conversation this week by asking someone a question.
Share one idea or opinion out loud.
Write down a moment when you made a difference to someone.

title: I have no confidence
example_phrases: I doubt myself all the time
I don't trust my own abilities

applications.ja-4-g: Confidence grows from small successes. Start with small steps.
applications.sen-104-25-a: Something is not impossible just because you have not done it yet.
applications.epi-ench-13-a: Growing means looking a bit foolish sometimes. That is fine.
applications.ja-2-e: Hard times show you what you can grow into.

exercise: Pick a small challenge you can do this week.
Do it, even nervously.
Write down that you did it.

title: People mock me for trying to improve
example_phrases: people laugh at my new lifestyle
friends tease me for trying to improve
they mock me for going to the gym
my family makes fun of my goals
people say I've changed and not in a good way
they think my dreams are silly

applications.epi-ench-22-a: When you change for the better, expect some mockery. Hold on to what you believe is right.
applications.sen-76-4-a: Mockery says more about their comfort than about your goals. You do not have to answer it.
applications.epi-ench-13-a: Looking foolish for a while is part of growing.
applications.sen-5-1-a: You are changing for yourself, not for their approval. Keep going quietly.

exercise: Keep your new habit quiet for a while if that helps.
Find one person who supports the change.
Remind yourself why you started.

title: I regret choices I made
example_phrases: I wish I could go back in time
I made the wrong choice years ago
I can't stop thinking about what could have been
if only I had done things differently

applications.ma-12-1-b: Let go of the past and act well in the present.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can begin again. It is within your reach.
applications.ma-7-29-a: Most of this pain lives in the past. Come back to now.
applications.epi-4-4-a: Notice how much you have learned since then.

exercise: Write down what you learned from that choice.
Ask: what can I do now with that lesson?
Do one small thing today that the wiser you would do.

title: Ashamed of something I did
example_phrases: I'm ashamed of what I did
I can't face people after what I did
I hurt someone and feel awful

applications.sen-53-8-a: Admitting a fault is a sign of waking up, not of weakness.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can start again from here.
applications.ma-10-8-a: Come back to the qualities you want to live by.
applications.ma-11-18-a: Everyone makes mistakes. You are human too.

exercise: If you hurt someone, consider a sincere apology.
Make amends where you can.
Then treat the lesson as your next step, not a life sentence.

title: I feel guilty for lying
example_phrases: I lied to someone I love
I was dishonest and feel terrible
I keep lying and hate it

applications.ma-12-17-a: Two simple rules for next time: if it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
applications.sen-28-9-a: Owning the lie, at least to yourself, is the first step to setting it right.
applications.sen-53-8-a: Feeling guilty shows your conscience is working.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can rebuild trust step by step.

exercise: Think about whether telling the truth now would help or hurt.
If it would help, tell them simply and apologise.
Decide what you will do differently next time.

title: I want to become a better person
example_phrases: I want to be a better person
I want to change for the better
I'm trying to grow as a person
I want to live with more integrity

applications.ma-10-16-a: You do not need a perfect plan to be better. Do one good thing today.
applications.ma-8-22-b: Start being better today, not tomorrow.
applications.epi-2-9-a: Be patient with yourself. It is a big task.
applications.sen-anger-3-36-a: End each day with a short review: what went better, what can improve.

exercise: Choose one quality to practise this week, like patience.
Each evening, note one moment you practised it.
Be kind about the moments you did not.

title: I relapsed into a bad habit
example_phrases: back to my old bad habit
I keep going back to it
I gave in after weeks of progress

applications.ma-5-9-a: You slipped. Do not give up in disgust; come back and keep going.
applications.ma-7-2-b: You can begin again right now.
applications.sen-29-8-a: Even interrupting a habit helps. Pauses grow into stopping.
applications.epi-4-4-a: The progress you made before the slip is still real.

exercise: Write down what triggered the relapse.
Plan what you will do next time that trigger comes.
Start again today; count the new days.

title: I drink too much
example_phrases: I think I have a drinking problem
alcohol is taking over my life

applications.sen-50-4-a: Problems like this are easier to treat early. Do not wait to ask for help.
applications.ma-7-7-a: Needing help is not weakness. Many people need support to change this.
applications.sen-29-8-a: Even small breaks from drinking are a real start.
applications.ma-5-31-a: You have come through hard things before. You can come through this.

exercise: Talk to a doctor or an addiction service about it.
Tell one person you trust what is going on.
Never stop heavy daily drinking suddenly on your own; it can be dangerous. Ask a doctor.

title: I spend hours on my phone
example_phrases: I can't put my phone down
I waste my life on my phone

applications.sen-1-1-a: Your time is yours. Take back the hours that slip away.
applications.sen-1-3-a: The hours on your phone come out of the only thing that is truly yours. Spend them on purpose.
applications.epi-ench-34-a: When the urge to scroll pulls, pause and picture how you will feel afterwards.
applications.epi-2-18-a: To break a habit, stop feeding it and practise something else instead.

exercise: Move social apps off your home screen.
Keep your phone out of the bedroom at night.
Choose something to do instead, like a book or a walk.

title: I can't get out of bed in the morning
example_phrases: I can't get out of bed
I have no energy to start the day
I stay in bed all morning
I don't want to wake up

applications.ma-5-1-a: Remind yourself why you are getting up: there is something only you can do today.
applications.ma-8-12-a: People are made to be useful to each other. Someone needs you today.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not face the whole day at once. Just the first step.
applications.sen-50-4-a: If this lasts for weeks with low mood, talk to a doctor.

exercise: Put your alarm across the room.
Plan one small thing to look forward to in the morning.
Do the first step only: sit up and put your feet on the floor.

title: Angry at myself for being lazy
example_phrases: I hate how unproductive I am
angry at myself for wasting the day

applications.epi-1-11-a: Change takes time. Be patient with yourself.
applications.sen-50-9-a: Starting is the hardest part. After that, it gets easier.
applications.ma-8-22-b: Do one small thing today instead of a big plan for tomorrow.
applications.ma-10-4-a: Blaming yourself does not help. Kindness gets you moving faster.

exercise: Pick one task that takes less than five minutes and do it now.
Notice that you did it.
Tomorrow, add one more.

title: I can't stick to a routine
example_phrases: I can't stick to a routine
I have no structure in my life
I give up on routines after a week

applications.epi-2-18-b: Every action strengthens some habit. Choose which ones you are building.
applications.sen-16-6-a: Keep at a good intention until it becomes a habit.
applications.epi-4-2-a: You cannot build many habits at once. Decide what matters and commit.
applications.ma-5-9-a: When you miss a day, just start again.

exercise: Choose one habit only.
Attach it to something you already do, like after coffee.
Track it for two weeks and forgive missed days.

title: I give up too easily
example_phrases: I quit when things get hard
as soon as it's difficult I stop

applications.ma-12-6-a: Keep practising even what feels hopeless. Skill grows with practice.
applications.ja-4-d: Strength grows through steady effort, like a muscle.
applications.sen-104-25-a: Something is not impossible just because you have not done it yet.
applications.epi-4-4-a: Look back and see how far you have already come.

exercise: When you want to quit, commit to five more minutes.
