Break the goal into smaller steps.
Celebrate finishing one step.

title: Starting is the hardest part
example_phrases: I don't know where to begin
I keep waiting for the right moment

applications.sen-50-9-a: Starting is the hardest part. Once you begin, it starts to feel good.
applications.ja-6-a: Great things start small, like an oak in an acorn.
applications.ma-3-14-a: Stop waiting for the perfect moment.
applications.epi-ench-4-a: Picture what the task involves, including the boring parts, so they do not stop you.

exercise: Define the very first, tiny action.
Do it for two minutes.
Stop or continue, your choice.

title: I keep buying things I don't need
example_phrases: my closet is full of things I never use
I spend money to feel better
my credit card is maxed out from shopping
I buy stuff and regret it

applications.epi-3-9-a: Want fewer things and you find you already have what you need.
applications.epi-ench-34-a: When the urge to buy pulls, pause and let the decision wait.
applications.sen-15-11-a: Many things look better from a distance than once you own them.
applications.ma-7-27-a: Notice what you already have and enjoy it.

exercise: Wait 48 hours before any non essential purchase.
Unsubscribe from shopping emails.
Notice what feeling you are trying to buy away.

title: I can't resist cravings
example_phrases: I eat junk food when stressed
I want it so badly I can't resist

applications.epi-ench-34-a: When a craving pulls, pause and picture how you will feel afterwards.
applications.sen-39-6-a: Moderation keeps pleasures enjoyable instead of ruling you.
applications.epi-2-18-e: Practise resisting small urges and you discover your strength.
applications.sen-29-8-a: Even delaying the craving helps. Pauses grow into control.

exercise: When a craving hits, wait ten minutes.
Drink water or take a short walk.
If you still want it, have a small amount slowly.

title: Worried about money or debt
example_phrases: I don't know how I'll pay rent

applications.epi-3-24-d: Being short of money is no shame. Keep fear from ruling you, and get practical help.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not carry all your money worries at once. Handle today's step.
applications.sen-65-24-a: Hardship can be borne. Do not let fear of it rule your life.
applications.ma-8-47-b: If something can be fixed, act instead of only worrying.

exercise: Write down what you owe and what comes in.
Contact a free debt advice service.
Pick one cost to cut this month.

title: I always want more money
example_phrases: I'm never satisfied with what I have
no matter how much I earn it's not enough

applications.sen-2-6-a: Poverty is about how much you crave. Wanting less makes you richer.
applications.sen-2-6-b: The right amount is first what you need, then what is enough.
applications.sen-16-9-a: The feeling of not having enough money may come from wants that have no limit, not from real needs.
applications.sen-59-14-a: Joy does not come from piling up more.

exercise: Write down what enough would look like for you.
Notice three things you already have and value.
Spend some money on an experience with someone you love.

title: Envy of people with more money
example_phrases: why do others have so much money
my friends are richer than me
seeing wealthy people makes me bitter
life is easier for the rich

applications.sen-94-7-a: Money does not make anyone happy. Plenty of rich people are miserable.
applications.epi-ench-44-a: Having more money does not make someone a better person.
applications.epi-ench-19-b: If your good is in your own choices, there is nothing to envy.
applications.sen-92-31-a: Fill your mind and heart. That is real wealth.

exercise: Notice the envy and name it.
Ask: what do I actually want, underneath the money?
Take one step toward that.

title: Ashamed of not having much
example_phrases: embarrassed that I don't have money
I can't afford what my friends can
I grew up poor and feel ashamed
I can't keep up with others financially

applications.epi-3-24-d: Being poor is no shame. Please also reach out for practical help.
applications.sen-1-5-a: If your needs are met, you are not poor in what matters. Shame is not a fair price for that.
applications.epi-ench-44-a: Your friends value you, not your bank balance. Your worth was never in what you own.
applications.sen-92-31-a: Real wealth is in your mind and heart.

exercise: Tell one trusted friend the truth about money.
Suggest free things to do together.
Look into support you may be entitled to.

title: I lost money
example_phrases: I lost money on an investment
I lost a lot of money
the stock market crash wiped me out
I was cheated out of money

applications.ma-8-17-a: Fix what you can, and let go of what you cannot.
applications.sen-helvia-5-a: Do not build your peace only on luck or money. Then losses shake you less.
applications.ma-5-31-a: Remember what you have already recovered from.
applications.sen-28-9-a: Learn the lesson, then move on.

exercise: Write down what happened and what you can recover.
If you were scammed, report it to the police and your bank.
Make one rule to prevent it next time.

title: My life changed suddenly
example_phrases: I wasn't ready for this change

applications.ma-9-21-a: Every stage of life ended when the next began, and you survived each change.
applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not face the whole change at once. Handle today.
applications.ma-5-20-a: What blocks the old path can become the way forward.

exercise: Write down what has changed and what has stayed the same.
Keep one small routine that grounds you.
Ask for help with the practical parts.

title: Moving to a new city or country
example_phrases: starting over in a new city

applications.ma-8-45-a: A new place does not have to change who you are.
applications.ma-5-16-b: Wherever you live, you can live well.
applications.ma-7-54-a: Wherever you are, you can accept it, treat people fairly and think clearly.
applications.sen-9-7-a: New friendships take time to grow. Start sowing.

exercise: Bring a few familiar things to make the new place yours.
Join one group or activity in the first month.
Stay in touch with home through regular calls.

title: Scared of a new chapter
example_phrases: graduating and entering the real world
entering a new phase of life

applications.ma-8-6-a: Change is familiar. You do not need to fear the new.
applications.ma-9-21-a: You have survived every change so far.
applications.sen-50-9-a: Starting is the hardest part; it gets easier.

exercise: Write down what excites you about this chapter, not only what scares you.
Pick one small first step.
Remind yourself of a past change you handled.

title: My plans fell apart
example_phrases: the trip I planned was cancelled

applications.ma-8-32-a: Circumstances may block your plans, but not your ability to act well.
applications.ma-5-20-a: The broken plan may point you to a different way forward you had not considered.
applications.epi-ench-26-a: Treat this like you would a friend's setback: real, but not a disaster.
applications.ma-10-22-a: You can adapt, change course, or finish your part with dignity.

exercise: Allow yourself to be disappointed for a while.
Write down what is still possible.
Make a new small plan.

title: My life isn't what I planned
example_phrases: my life isn't what I expected
this is not where I thought I'd be
disappointed with how my life turned out
I expected more from my life

applications.ma-7-57-a: The life you have is the one you can actually love. The planned one only exists in your head.
applications.ma-5-16-b: Your life does not have to match the plan to be a good one.
applications.epi-ench-17-b: You did not choose how things turned out, but you can choose how you live from here.
applications.ja-2-e: This shows you who you are, and what you can still grow into.

exercise: Write down three good things in your life you did not plan.
Name one thing you still want, and one step toward it.
Talk to someone about it.

title: Everything goes wrong for me
example_phrases: bad things always happen to me
why does this always happen to me

applications.ma-4-49-b: Instead of 'I am unlucky', try 'I am lucky that I can bear it'.
applications.epi-3-3-a: Much of what we call bad luck is our opinion about it.
applications.ma-8-15-a: Expect some trouble in life. Then each one shakes you less.
applications.epi-ench-43-a: Look for the handle you can hold in each situation.

exercise: Write down this week's bad events and one good one.
For each bad one, name one thing you can do.
Do the smallest one today.

title: Stuck in a rut
example_phrases: my life is boring and repetitive

applications.ja-2-f: Changing yourself is the part of the change most within reach.
applications.ma-7-2-b: A rut is not permanent. One small change today is a new beginning.
applications.sen-101-10-a: Treat each day as a whole life. Do something new in it.
applications.ja-6-b: Change can start inside: a new habit or way of thinking often moves the rest.

exercise: Change one small thing tomorrow: a new route, a new food, a new person.
Pick one thing you used to enjoy and try it again.
Plan one bigger change for this month.

title: Retiring and not sure what's next
example_phrases: I just retired and feel lost
what do I do now that I'm retired
retirement is harder than I thought
I don't know who I am without my job

applications.sen-12-4-a: Growing older has its own pleasures if you use the years well.
applications.sen-60-4-a: Being useful to others is what it means to really live.
applications.sen-13-17-a: Do not spend your time getting ready to live. Start now.
applications.ma-4-23-a: Retirement is a new season, with its own fruit to discover.

exercise: Try one new activity or class this month.
Offer your experience to someone who needs it.
Build a loose weekly routine.

title: I don't know my purpose
example_phrases: what is the point of life
I don't know what I want

applications.ja-4-c: You do not need to know your life's purpose to have a good day. Do today's task well and see where it leads.
applications.sen-60-4-a: Being useful to others gives life meaning.
applications.ma-8-26-a: There is deep satisfaction in being kind and understanding the world.
applications.ja-4-b: Even a small aim gives your mind somewhere better to go.

exercise: Write down three moments you felt most alive.
Ask what they have in common.
Try one small thing in that direction this week.

title: I feel like I'm wasting my life
example_phrases: I feel like I'm wasting time
I should be doing more with my life

applications.sen-shortness-1-a: Your life is not too short; the days just slip by unused. You can start using them on purpose today.
applications.sen-93-3-a: Aim to live fully, not only to be alive.
applications.sen-1-1-a: Reclaim your time. It is yours.
applications.ma-8-22-b: Do not plan to change tomorrow. Start today.

exercise: Write down what a well used day would look like for you.
Do one part of that day tomorrow.
Cut one thing that wastes your time.

title: Waiting for my real life to start
example_phrases: I'll be happy when things change
waiting for my real life to start
someday I'll do what I love
I'm always waiting for the right time
life will begin after I finish this

applications.sen-shortness-9-b: Waiting loses today while it depends on tomorrow.
applications.ma-12-1-a: The peace you hope for someday is available now, if you stop postponing it.
applications.sen-shortness-3-b: Do not save what matters for later in life. Begin it now.
applications.epi-ench-50-b: You do not need permission or perfect conditions to start living the way you want.

exercise: Name one thing you keep saying you will do someday.
Do a small version of it this week.
Notice how it feels to stop waiting.

title: Too busy to breathe
example_phrases: busy every minute of the day
I never have time for what matters

applications.ma-8-51-a: Being always busy is not a badge of honour. Make room to breathe, even ten minutes.
applications.sen-3-5-a: A full calendar does not mean a full life. Check which tasks actually matter.
applications.ma-4-24-b: Ask of each task: is this necessary?
applications.sen-1-3-a: Your time is the one thing that is truly yours. Guard it.

exercise: Look at your week and cross out one thing.
Block 30 minutes a day with nothing planned.
Say no to one new request.

title: Time is flying by
example_phrases: I can't believe how fast time passes

applications.sen-49-2-a: Notice how fast the last year went, and choose one thing to make this one count.
applications.ma-3-10-a: This moment is the one you can actually live.
applications.sen-101-10-a: Make each day full enough that it feels like a life of its own.
applications.ma-2-14-a: Time feels fast when we live elsewhere. Being present today makes it feel full.

exercise: Tonight, write one sentence about today that you want to remember.
Plan one meaningful thing for this week.
Put your phone away during one meal a day.

title: I'm bored with everything
example_phrases: I lost interest in my hobbies

applications.sen-93-3-a: It is possible to be alive without really living. Aim to live fully.
applications.sen-anger-2-20-a: Play and light fun are good for the mind.
applications.ma-8-26-a: Learning and kindness bring deep satisfaction.
applications.sen-89-23-a: Learn to go deeper into something, not just wider.

exercise: Try one thing you have never done this week.
Learn something new for 15 minutes a day.
Do something kind for someone.

title: Questioning my life in midlife
example_phrases: rethinking my whole life at fifty
what have I done with my life
I want to change everything in my forties

applications.ma-7-56-a: Imagine your life so far is complete, and treat each day from now as a bonus to live well.
applications.sen-93-3-a: Aim to live fully from here on.
applications.ma-10-1-a: When will you finally live simply and honestly? Why not begin today?
applications.sen-70-6-a: What matters is not how long you live, but how well.

exercise: Write down what you want the next ten years to be about.
Find one change you can start now.
Talk about it with someone you trust.

title: Success is going to my head
example_phrases: people say I've changed since I got rich

applications.ma-8-33-a: Enjoy the promotion, but remember it can change. Your character is what lasts.
applications.ma-6-30-a: Success can change people. Keep returning to simple goodness.
applications.epi-ench-6-a: Take pride only in how you act, not in what you have.
applications.sen-5-1-a: Success is a chance to keep improving, not a reason to stop.

exercise: Thank the people who helped you get here.
Ask a trusted friend to tell you honestly if you change.
Do something humble this week.

title: Nobody thanks me or appreciates what I do
example_phrases: I help everyone and get nothing

applications.ma-11-4-a: Doing good is its own reward. It counts without thanks.
applications.ma-7-73-a: Once someone has benefited, the good is complete.
applications.ma-7-74-a: Your help made a difference, even without thanks, and it is good for you as well.
applications.ma-8-56-a: Your peace does not have to depend on their gratitude. You can also say what you need.

exercise: Notice the help you give and value it yourself.
Tell someone calmly that a thank you would mean a lot.
Make sure you are not giving more than you can.

title: Afraid of losing what I have
example_phrases: afraid of losing what I have
scared it will all go away
my life is good and I fear losing it
worried about losing my job, my partner, everything
I can't enjoy happiness because I fear it will end
fear of losing my loved ones

applications.sen-98-6-a: Fearing a loss can hurt as much as the loss. Enjoy what you have now.
applications.sen-marcia-10-a: Love what you have fully, knowing nothing lasts forever.
applications.ma-2-14-b: Only the present is really yours. Live in it.
applications.sen-110-4-a: Do not cling too hard, and loss will not hold you as tightly.

exercise: When the fear comes, name what you are grateful for right now.
Spend fully present time with the people you love.
Remind yourself that you have handled change before.

title: I reached my goal and feel empty
example_phrases: I achieved my goal and feel empty
I got what I wanted and still feel nothing
after the big win I feel lost
what now after reaching my dream

applications.sen-59-14-a: Joy does not come from achievements alone.
applications.ma-8-26-a: Satisfaction comes from being kind and understanding the world.
applications.sen-15-11-a: Many things look better from a distance than once you have them.
applications.sen-60-4-a: Being useful to others can fill what achievements cannot.

exercise: Let yourself rest after the goal.
Ask: what did I enjoy on the way there?
Find a next aim that is about people or growth, not only results.

title: Someone criticized my creative work

applications.ma-6-21-a: If some of the criticism is true, it can make your work better.
applications.ma-4-20-a: Praise does not make your work better and blame does not make it worse. Its worth is in itself.
applications.ma-5-3-a: If you believe in your work, do not let criticism stop you.
applications.epi-ench-42-a: Critics usually believe they are right. That does not make them right.

exercise: Wait a day before reading the criticism again.
Pick out one useful point, if there is one.
Keep making your work.

title: I'm getting older and it scares me

applications.sen-12-4-a: Growing older has its own pleasures if you use the years well.
applications.ma-4-23-a: Getting older brings its own gifts: experience, perspective and calm.
applications.sen-70-6-a: What matters is not how long you live, but how well.
applications.ma-9-21-a: You have moved through every stage of life so far.

exercise: Write down three things that are better now than when you were younger.
Take care of your body with one small habit.
Spend time with people of different ages.

title: A milestone birthday got me down
example_phrases: another birthday and I feel old
I'm turning fifty and feel sad
I don't want to celebrate my birthday

applications.sen-12-4-a: Each age has its own pleasures.
applications.sen-101-10-a: Treat each day as a whole life, starting today.
applications.ma-6-56-a: Each year you have is not to be taken for granted.
applications.ma-7-56-a: Treat the years ahead as a gift to live well.

exercise: Celebrate in a way that feels right to you, even small.
Write down what you want this next year to be about.
Thank someone who made the last years better.

title: I'm afraid of dying
example_phrases: the thought of dying terrifies me
I'm afraid of my own death

applications.ma-12-35-a: If you value living well over living long, death loses much of its terror.
applications.sen-70-6-a: Instead of fearing the end, focus on living well in the time you have.
applications.ma-9-3-a: Seeing death as part of life's natural course can make it less frightening.
applications.epi-2-1-a: Often the fear torments us more than the thing itself.

exercise: When the fear comes, breathe and name it: this is fear.
Turn it into a question: how do I want to live today?
If the fear takes over your days, talk to a therapist.

title: Thinking a lot about mortality
example_phrases: I think about mortality a lot
we're all going to die someday
how do I live knowing I will die

applications.ma-2-11-a: Let the shortness of life sharpen what you do today, rather than frighten you.
applications.ma-4-17-a: Knowing life ends is a reason to live as the person you want to be, starting now.
applications.sen-78-27-a: A short life can still be full of good.
applications.sen-70-6-a: What matters is how well, not how long.

exercise: Write down what you would regret not doing.
Do one of those things this month.
Tell someone you love what they mean to you.

title: The news makes me anxious or angry
example_phrases: I can't stop reading bad news
the state of the world upsets me

applications.epi-3-18-a: The news is outside your control; your response is not.
applications.ma-2-7-a: When events pull you in every direction, step back and learn something worthwhile.
applications.ma-8-49-a: Separate what was reported from the commentary and fear around it. The facts alone are easier to hold.
applications.ma-6-52-a: You do not have to have an opinion about everything.

exercise: Limit news to once or twice a day.
Turn off news notifications.
Do one small helpful thing locally.

title: The world feels unfair
example_phrases: bad people get away with everything
good people suffer while bad people win
why is the world so cruel

applications.ma-9-42-a: There will always be people who behave badly. Expecting otherwise only adds anger.
applications.ma-8-17-a: Fix what you can, and let go of what you cannot.
applications.ma-8-32-a: Unfairness cannot stop you from acting fairly yourself.
applications.ma-6-54-a: Your good and others' good are linked. Small fair acts matter.

exercise: Pick one cause you care about.
Give it some time or money each month.
Treat the people around you fairly today.

title: I feel powerless to change things
example_phrases: the problems are too big for me
I have no control over my life
what difference can one person make

applications.epi-1-1-d: Others may limit your circumstances, but your will stays your own.
applications.epi-4-13-a: Put your care into your choices, which no one can block.
applications.ma-8-17-a: Fix what you can, and let go of the rest.
applications.epi-2-5-a: Separate what you control from what you do not, then act on the first.

exercise: Write two lists: what I control and what I do not.
Do one thing from the first list today.
Let the second list go, for now.

title: Worried about climate change
example_phrases: I'm scared for the future of the earth
what kind of world will my kids live in

applications.epi-2-5-a: Separate what you can do from what you cannot.
applications.sen-13-10-b: The future is not written yet; people are working on it, and you can too.
applications.ma-8-5-a: First, do not panic. Then look steadily at what you can do.
applications.ma-6-54-a: What helps the community helps you. Small actions add up.

exercise: Choose one or two climate actions that fit your life.
Join others who care; acting together eases worry.
Limit doom reading and spend time in nature.

title: I put it off because it has to be perfect
example_phrases: I can't start until I know it will be perfect
I keep redoing the first line and never finish
if I can't do it perfectly I don't do it at all
I wait for the perfect moment to begin
my standards are so high I never get started
I polish things forever instead of finishing

applications.sen-shortness-9-b: Waiting for perfect conditions loses today. A rough start now beats a perfect start never.
applications.epi-1-15-a: Good work ripens over time. The first draft is allowed to be unripe.
applications.ma-5-9-a: Mistakes will happen. Come back and improve instead of not starting.
applications.sen-50-9-a: Once you begin, it starts to feel good.

exercise: Give yourself permission to make a bad first version.
Set a timer for 20 minutes and aim for done, not perfect.
Improve it later, in a second pass.

title: I avoid starting because I'm afraid it will go badly
example_phrases: I avoid the task because I'm scared of failing
fear makes me put things off
I don't start because it might go wrong
I avoid opening the document because it makes me anxious
the thought of doing it badly freezes me
I put off hard things because they scare me
I'd rather not try than try and fail

applications.sen-82-19-a: Fears you avoid quietly hold you back. Facing them a little at a time sets you free.
applications.sen-13-4-a: The task you imagine is usually worse than the real one.
applications.epi-3-26-a: Courage grows each time you act despite the fear.
applications.sen-shortness-9-c: The future is uncertain anyway. Begin now and learn as you go.

exercise: Name the exact fear in one sentence.
Do the smallest, least scary part first, for five minutes.
Notice afterwards how it compared to what you feared.

title: A big project feels too big to start
example_phrases: the project is so big I don't know where to start
writing a whole book feels impossible
the size of the job paralyses me
I have a big report and keep putting it off
too much to do so I do nothing

applications.ma-8-36-a: Do not carry the whole project at once. Do today's piece.
applications.ja-6-a: Every big thing starts small, like an oak from an acorn.
applications.ma-3-12-a: Give the one piece in front of you your full attention.
applications.sen-shortness-9-a: Putting it off only takes away the days you could use. Start a small part now.

exercise: Break the project into pieces of under one hour.
Write the first three pieces on a list.
Do the first one today.

title: I keep avoiding emails, bills and admin
example_phrases: I have hundreds of unread emails
I keep avoiding paying my bills
I put off calling the doctor or the bank
paperwork piles up and I ignore it
my to do list of small chores never shrinks

applications.epi-1-6-b: Small annoying tasks are usually easier to deal with than to keep avoiding.
applications.ma-8-47-b: If you can fix it, act instead of worrying about it.
applications.sen-shortness-8-a: Every hour spent dreading a task is time you never get back.
applications.sen-50-9-a: Starting is the hardest part; the rest is often quick.

exercise: Set a timer for 15 minutes and clear as many small tasks as you can.
Start with the one you dread most; it is often the fastest.
Do a short session like this every day at the same time.

title: I stay up too late to get time for myself
example_phrases: I stay up scrolling even though I'm tired
I don't want the day to end so I stay awake
I sleep too little because night is my only free time
I keep saying one more episode
I go to bed at 2am every night
I know I should sleep but I keep delaying it

applications.sen-1-1-a: Take back your time during the day, so you do not have to steal it from your sleep.
applications.ma-8-51-a: A life with no room to breathe pushes us to grab time at night. Make room earlier.
applications.epi-ench-34-a: When the urge for one more video comes, pause and picture how you will feel tomorrow.
applications.sen-15-6-a: Your mind needs rest that truly restores it.

exercise: Plan 30 minutes of real me time earlier in the evening.
Set a phone alarm one hour before bed to start winding down.
Charge your phone outside the bedroom.

title: I feel guilty about all the time I wasted
example_phrases: I wasted the whole day and feel terrible
I hate myself for wasting so much time
I'm ashamed of how much I put off
I feel bad every evening about what I didn't do

applications.sen-shortness-2-a: Life is long enough if you use it well from here on.
applications.ma-10-4-a: Blaming yourself does not help. Kindness gets you moving faster.
applications.ma-8-22-b: Do one small thing now instead of a big plan for tomorrow.

exercise: Forgive yourself for yesterday in one sentence.
Choose one small task to do in the next hour.
Tonight, notice that you did it.
